title: Person tombstones in ClickHouse and the ordered sweep
answers: How are deleted persons tombstoned in ClickHouse?
Why does the cleanup sweep delete in two passes?
How is a revived person handled?
body:
- Soft delete: `_delete_person` (posthog/models/person/util.py) writes `is_deleted=True` at version+100; `split_person` uses +101 to override deletes; plugin-server generateKafkaPersonUpdateMessage must stay in sync with the offset. `delete_person` also tombstones each distinct id via `_delete_ch_distinct_id`.
- Deleted-ness = `argMax(is_deleted, version)`, never 'any row deleted' (`_LIVE_PERSONS_BASE` in models/person/deletion.py; `DeletedPersonsTable` in dags/clickhouse_cleanup.py).
- Revive (deletion.py `reset_all_deleted_person_distinct_ids`, `_reset_person_in_clickhouse`): raise versions +100 (default 2500) and raise PG floors via SetPersonVersionFloor/SetPersonDistinctIdVersionFloor (never lower).
- Sweep `_run_ordered_delete`: first delete versions below snapshot max (`below_max`), then max; never merged, bounded by snapshot max_version.
- Sweep uses run_id-scoped snapshot tables (posthog/clickhouse/cleanup_snapshots); `_require_snapshot_intact` fails if 14-day TTL shrank one; `recheck_revived_persons` runs before distinct id and person deletes.
